Show HN: Terminal Gym – a Claude mod that makes you do pushups between prompts
items.summary: Hi HN, I built this for myself and wanted to open-source it. The problem: I wanted a way to get reminders in-between prompts as I often spend long hours in the terminal, especially now that we're usually parallel-processing so many agents. The first version was a simple rep counter in my Claude Code status line and a shell script to log reps. Since Claude Code shipped mods this week, I thought this was a good way to level it up with even more accountability. How it works: 1. Every day, you get a daily goal for either squats, pushups, or dips (e.g. 0/100 pushups) with +5 / +10 / +25 buttons to log a set in the terminal. 2. Reminders for sets are spread out across the day so it doesn't get annoying, starting from your first prompt for the day. A toast tells you when the next set is due. 3. Strict mode is opt-in: if you're falling behind in terms of your daily rep goal, it will block your prompts till you log some reps. Added a streak counter for some added fun. All local and data is stored as plain files in ~/.claude/fitness. Install: claude plugin marketplace add DrumAndCode/terminal-gym && claude plugin install terminal-gym@terminal-gym Overall, thought the mod API is super powerful and can't wait to see the stuff people build with it. Eg: I built a clickable onboarding process inside the terminal, and that felt quite powerful to use. Now you can enjoy spending both tokens and calories. :)

items.title: Show HN: I made a browser-based instrument out of the CHOMPI CLUB source
items.summary: A few days ago Chase Bliss open sourced the CHOMPI Club source code under an MIT license https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49912048 so I've been working on an AU/VST3/AAX plug-in. The plug-in includes all the samples so it's a bit heavy, so I decided to add WASM as a compilation target and compile it directly for the browser. I've built an interactive tutorial and added UX enhancements to make editing it easier. For those of you who don't know, the CHOMPI Club started off as a Kickstarter https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/chompiclub/chompi-a-mag... I bought one, and I absolutely love it. The CHOMPI development team was acqu-hired by Chase Bliss (who is a small team that makes incredible, premium guitar pedals), and for reasons unknown they decided to shelf the project and make the code open. https://github.com/CHOMPI-Club/CHOMPI/ I think they intended other makers to build Daisy seed hardware out of it, but I want to show people how awesome an instrument this is so my goal is to not only make it accessible but to make the UX better and build tutorials around the various modes. Let people play it on the web and download it as a free plug-in if they like it. Right now, TAPE mode is supported but TEMPO and WAVE modes are working on my development machine and I'm just testing them. I've been working on this for the past few days all day with GPT 6 Astra Max on /ultrafast. Right now, we're modelling an Akai S950 circuit to swap out the native CHOMPI sampler code with as an option and we've downloaded data sheets, schematics, and spent 10 hours on testing and getting it in top shape. Have fun! Feel free to ask any questions. - Not associated with Chase Bliss or CHOMPI Club
